items.headline: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
items.detail: Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.

items.headline: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
items.detail: A Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather won a U.S. military contract worth almost $50 million.

items.headline: The Social Reckoning is flopping at the box office
items.detail: As important as some of the messages in The Social Reckoning are, the movie has been drastically underperforming at the box office.

items.headline: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
items.detail: Meta is making up for lost time in the AI race. After launching Muse Spark, the first model from its revamped Superintelligence Labs division, and buzzy AI agent Muse, it's now launching two new models it claims can go toe-to-toe with the…

items.headline: Cyber attack hits hundreds of French supermarkets, heating fridges to 122°F and sparking fires
items.detail: Hackers targeted hundreds of French supermarkets in a large-scale cyberattack, causing refrigerators to overheat, spoiling food, and sparking fires.

items.headline: IMF warns bond yields could see a 'disorderly' spike as debt, inflation risks worsen
items.detail: The IMF says risks in the government bond market have worsened and that yields could jump sharply and disorderly.

items.headline: Bumble shares soar after report dating firm in $1bn takeover talks
items.detail: The jump pushed Bumble's stock market valuation to more than $580m but that is still far below their peak of more than $14bn.

items.headline: AI minister warns 'likely' UK's cyber defences will be breached
items.detail: Kanishka Narayan said the government will use advanced AI to strengthen the UK against cyber attacks.

items.headline: Mainland Chinese traders boost Hong Kong stock buying for fourth month as AI bets surge
items.detail: Mainland Chinese investors bought more Hong Kong stocks than they sold for a fourth consecutive month in September, with purchases accelerating despite persistent headwinds from elevated US Treasury yields and oil prices.
